finding: CNN and Transformer architectures have different memory drivers.
evidence: CNN memory depends heavily on image resolution, channels, feature maps, and batch size; Transformer memory depends on sequence length, embedding size, attention heads, and feed-forward blocks.
why_it_matters: A single memory estimator may not generalize across architectures without architecture-aware features.

finding: The simple Transformer has much higher parameter memory than the simple CNN.
evidence: The Transformer fp32 parameter memory is about 116.79x the CNN fp32 parameter memory.
why_it_matters: Embedding layers and Transformer blocks can dominate parameter memory even in small Transformer-style models.

finding: Attention-based models require sequence-length-aware memory estimation.
evidence: Transformer memory depends on token sequence length and attention computation.
why_it_matters: This supports the need for separate handling of sequence length in LLM memory estimation.

finding: CNN-style workloads need image-resolution and feature-map-aware estimation.
evidence: CNN activations are spatial tensors whose size depends on height, width, channels, and batch size.
why_it_matters: Vision-style models require different memory features than text Transformer models.

finding: Day 56 is a setup day for architecture comparison.
evidence: Simple CNN and Transformer models were defined, parameter memory was compared, and optional forward profiling was added.
why_it_matters: This creates the foundation for deeper architecture comparison in the next days.
